Uses of Package
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.domain.mfa

Packages that use com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.domain.mfa
Package
Description
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.mfa
Multi-factor authentication orchestration.
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.ott
One-time token authentication: e-mail and SMS codes and magic links as a primary sign-in method and as a second factor, the per-channel factors, the rate limits, the providers and filters, and the phone management API and account page.
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.passkeys
Passkeys (WebAuthn): the factor, the chain wiring, the login and second-factor fragments, the account API and the account page.
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.social
Social login (identity brokering) through external identity providers: Google, Microsoft Entra ID, Apple and GitHub.
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.totp
Time-based one-time password (TOTP) second factor.
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.x509
X.509 client certificate authentication: a certificate presented on a dedicated TLS port, or forwarded by a trusted reverse proxy in a header, signs in the user it is bound to (by the SHA-256 fingerprint of the certificate) at POST /login/x509, the form of the login page, with the CSRF token.
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.application.mfa
Use cases of the multi-factor framework: security events, second-factor lockout and trusted devices.
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.application.passkeys
Use cases that manage the passkeys (WebAuthn credentials) of a user: list, rename and delete, whether the user has one (a second factor enrolment query), and the relying party settings.
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.application.sms
Use cases of the SMS channel: phone enrolment and verification, cost-capped sending of codes and the enrolment query of the SMS second factor.
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.application.totp
Use cases of the TOTP authenticator-app second factor and its recovery codes.
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.domain.mfa
Multi-factor authentication: the authentication factors, the policy that decides when an authentication is strong enough, trusted devices, the audit trail and the failed-attempt lockout of the second factor.
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.infrastructure.keys
Signing keys of the authorization server: key encryption and generation, the JWK sources and the signed token service built on them.
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.infrastructure.persistence.mfa
PostgreSQL implementations of the multi-factor ports: security events, second-factor attempts and the per-user enforcement flag, over the security_events, second_factor_attempts and users tables.

    Port that signs the value of the trusted-device cookie and checks that signature, so a value the server did not issue is rejected before anything is looked up.
